beats.lead: The Game Boy that 'survived a bomb' was declared a lost cause.
beats.text: Its front was burned and melted in its owner's barracks during a bombing in the Gulf War.
beats.note: Its owner, Stephan Scoggins, a medic deployed in the war, posted it to Nintendo Power asking for a replacement.

beats.text: Nintendo's technicians wrote it off, then found it still powered on. Start and Select still worked, so they tested it with Tetris.
beats.note: That is all the source confirms: not that every button and the screen survived.

beats.name: Nintendo Power issue 26
beats.role: printed his letter and sent him a new Game Boy 'as a special Desert Storm courtesy'

beats.text: The scorched console went on show in Nintendo's New York store, switched on and playing Tetris.
beats.note: Keeping it running took new batteries and, at one point, a replacement screen.

beats.text: In 2023 a store worker confirmed it had been quietly sent back to Nintendo of America's headquarters in Redmond, Washington.
beats.note: It is unclear whether it will ever go back on show.

beats.line: The toughest Game Boy ever needed a new screen.
